Announces Financial and Operating Results for the Three and Nine-Month Periods Ended September 30, 2026 and Declares Dividend of $0.13 per Share Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, November 4, 2026 / PRNewswire/ – SandRidge Energy, Inc. (the “Company” or “SandRidge”) (NYSE: SD) today announced financial and operational results for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. Recent Highlights • On November 3, 2026, the Board declared a dividend of $0.13 per share of the Company's common stock, payable on November 30, 2026 to stockholders of record on November 19, 2026. Stockholders can elect to receive the dividends in cash or additional shares of common stock by enrolling in the Company’s previously announced Dividend Reinvestment Plan • Production averaged 20.9 MBoe per day during the third quarter, an increase of 10% on a Boe basis versus the same period in 2025. Oil production increased 8% and total revenues increased 37% during the quarter versus the same period in 2025, driven primarily by new production from our operated development program, higher commodity prices, and recently acquired assets for a portion of the quarter • Third quarter net income of $30.6 million, or $0.83 per basic share. Adjusted net income (1) of $23.8 million or $0.64 per basic share • Adjusted EBITDA (1) of $39.3 million for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026 • In the first nine months of 2026, the Company successfully completed seven gross wells as part of its ongoing one-rig Cherokee development program • During the third quarter, the Company closed its previously announced acquisition of certain producing assets and leasehold interests in the Cherokee Play, expanding its efficient operations in the area with the addition of ~7,000 net leasehold acres, interests in 21 wells, and eight proven development locations • As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $70.0 million of cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash • Despite a growing asset base, SandRidge maintained best-in-class administrative costs, with adjusted G&A (1) of $1.8 million, or $0.94 per Boe for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026 Grayson Pranin, SandRidge’s President, Chief Executive Officer & Director, commented on the quarter: “The Company continues to increase production versus last year, driven by our one-rig program in the Cherokee Play and the closing of the previously announced bolt-on acquisition, extending our efficient operations in the area. I continue to be amazed by the team's record of five years without a recordable safety incident while maintaining a low G&A burden and folding new assets into the portfolio. The Company has benefited from strong WTI prices this past quarter and year, with current WTI futures providing a potential tailwind through the end of the year and into next. This provides a positive backdrop for integrating the new assets into our development plans." 1 Financial Results Dollars in thousands (except per share data) 3Q26 2Q26 Change vs 2Q26 3Q25 Change vs 3Q25 Net income $ 30,615 $ 26,693 $ 3,922 $ 15,953 $ 14,662 Net Income per share $ 0.83 $ 0.72 $ 0.11 $ 0.44 $ 0.39 Net cash provided by operating activities $ 32,131 $ 42,436 $ (10,305) $ 25,269 $ 6,862 Adjusted net income (1) $ 23,795 $ 20,973 $ 2,822 $ 15,478 $ 8,317 Adjusted net income per share (1) $ 0.64 $ 0.57 $ 0.07 $ 0.42 $ 0.22 Adjusted operating cash flow (1) $ 39,344 $ 34,571 $ 4,773 $ 27,933 $ 11,411 Adjusted EBITDA (1) $ 39,309 $ 34,033 $ 5,276 $ 27,285 $ 12,024 Free cash flow (1) $ 10,475 $ 23,241 $ (12,766) $ 5,919 $ 4,556 Operational Results & Update Production, Revenue, & Realized Prices 3Q26 2Q26 Change vs 2Q26 3Q25 Change vs 3Q25 Production MBoe 1,922 1,797 125 1,745 177 MBoed 20.9 19.7 1.2 19.0 1.9 Oil as percentage of production 19% 18% 1% 20% (1)% Natural gas as percentage of production 50% 50% —% 48% 2% NGLs as percentage of production 31% 32% (1)% 32% (1)% Revenues Oil, natural gas and NGL revenues $54,416 $51,117 $3,299 $39,822 $14,594 Oil as percentage of revenues 58% 61% (3)% 56% 2% Natural gas as percentage of revenues 17% 14% 3% 22% (5)% NGLs as percentage of revenues 25% 25% —% 22% 3% Realized Prices Realized oil price per barrel $85.27 $95.35 $(10.08) $65.23 $20.04 Realized natural gas price per Mcf $1.62 $1.36 $0.26 $1.71 $(0.09) Realized NGL price per barrel $22.68 $21.68 $1.00 $15.61 $7.07 Realized price per Boe $28.32 $28.45 $(0.13) $22.82 $5.50 Production volumes continue to benefit from the Company's ongoing drilling program, efficient production operations, and recently acquired assets which impacted a portion of the third quarter. Third quarter Boe production increased by approximately 10% versus the same period in 2025 and increased by approximately 7% versus the prior quarter. Oil production increased by approximately 8% relative to the same period last year and increased by approximately 13% versus the prior quarter. Revenues increased by 6% in the third quarter versus the second quarter of 2026 and 37% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Realized price per Boe improved in the third quarter versus the same period last year and was slightly below the second quarter 2026 due to lower oil pricing quarter-over-quarter. 2 Drilling & Completion Operations As of September 30, 2026, the Company completed seven new gross operated wells as part of its ongoing one-rig Cherokee development program. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, drilling, completion and capital workover spend was $57.3 million. Operating Costs During the third quarter of 2026, lease operating expense ("LOE") was $11.0 million or $5.75 per Boe versus $10.3 million or $5.73 per Boe during the prior quarter. Third quarter LOE per Boe remained consistent versus the second quarter, while expenses from the recently acquired assets in the Cherokee Play contributed to an increase in absolute LOE. Third quarter LOE per Boe decreased by approximately 8% when compared to the same period in 2025. Liquidity & Capital Structure As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $70.0 million of cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash of $1.3 million, deposited with multiple, well-capitalized financial institutions. The Company had no outstanding term or revolving debt obligations as of September 30, 2026. Stockholders interested in participating in the DRIP or seeking additional information may contact their broker or Equiniti Trust Company, LLC, the Plan Administrator, at (800) 278-4353 or https://equiniti.com/us/ast-access/individuals. Share Repurchases No shares were repurchased during the third quarter of 2026, but the Company maintains its ability to opportunistically repurchase shares under its 10b5-1 program. Since inception of the program, the Company has repurchased 0.6 million shares at an average price of $10.75 per share. Of the $75.0 million repurchase authorization, $68.3 million remained as of September 30, 2026. 3 Outlook We remain committed to growing the value of our asset base in a safe, responsible and efficient manner, while prudently allocating capital to high-return, growth projects. Currently, these projects include: (1) one-rig development in the Cherokee Play (2) evaluation of accretive merger and acquisition opportunities, with consideration of our strong balance sheet and commitment to our capital return program (3) production optimization program through artificial lift conversions to more efficient and cost-effective systems and (4) a leasing program that will bolster future development and extend development in our Cherokee assets. We are developing our term acreage in the Cherokee Play, and our total leasehold position, inclusive of the Cherokee, NW Stack and legacy assets, is approximately 95% held by production. We will continue to monitor forward-looking commodity prices, project results, costs and other factors that could influence returns and cash flows, and will adjust our program accordingly, to include curtailment of capital activity and wells, if needed, or conversely, well reactivations in higher natural gas price environments. These and other factors, including reasonable reinvestment rates, maintaining our cash flows and prioritizing our regular-way dividend, will continue to shape our development decisions for 2026 and beyond. Environmental, Social, & Governance ("ESG") SandRidge maintains its Environmental, Social, and Governance ("ESG") commitment to harvesting the Company's resources in a safe and environmentally conscious manner, to include no routine flaring of produced natural gas, transporting nearly 90% of our produced water via pipeline instead of truck, and powering nearly all of our well sites with electricity, mitigating the need for less efficient power sources. Via a 24-hour manned operations center and dedicated personnel trained in the use of infrared leak detection and other specialized equipment, the Company continually monitors our asset base for potential emissions and continually works to optimize efficiency through initiatives such as proactive artificial lift upgrades that reduce SandRidge's electric power consumption. Additionally, SandRidge maintains an emphasis on the safety and training of our workforce with a demonstrable safety track record, including five years without a recordable safety incident, as integral to our culture. The Company has personnel dedicated to the close monitoring of our safety standards and daily operations. Financial Measures This press release includes non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP measures are not alternatives to GAAP measures, and you should not consider these non-GAAP measures in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Below is additional disclosure regarding each of the non-GAAP measures used in this press release, including reconciliations to their most directly comparable GAAP measure. Reconciliation of Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities to Adjusted Operating Cash Flow The Company defines adjusted operating cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities before changes in operating assets and liabilities as shown in the following table. Adjusted operating cash flow is a supplemental financial measure used by the Company's management and by securities analysts, investors, lenders, rating agencies and others who follow the industry as an indicator of the Company's ability to internally fund exploration and development activities or incur new debt. The Company also uses this measure because operating cash flow relates to the timing of cash receipts and disbursements that the Company may not control and may not relate to the period in which the operating activities occurred. Further, adjusted operating cash flow allows the Company to compare its operating performance and return on capital with those of other companies without regard to financing methods and capital structure. This measure should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for net cash provided by operating activities prepared in accordance with GAAP.
